item.title: Seshadri's desingularisation in the Hodge diamond cutter, and a bold proposal
item.description:
The functionality outlined below, and much more, is implemented in Hodge diamond cutter, which can be used in Sage. If you use it for your research, please cite it using .

As I was cleaning up things I ran into my print-out of del Baño: On the motive of moduli spaces of rank two vector bundles over a curve, which I apparently printed on December 15, 2017. This marks the start of my interest in these moduli spaces (which have an extremely rich and beautiful history!) and I noticed I never really looked at Section 3. In this section the Hodge numbers for Seshadri's desingularisation of $\mathrm{M}_C(2,\mathcal{O}_C)$ are computed, and I couldn't resist having a little fun with this.

item.title: Quiver moduli in the Hodge diamond cutter
item.description:
The functionality outlined below, and much more, is implemented in Hodge diamond cutter, which can be used in Sage. If you use it for your research, please cite it using .

Another family of varieties has been added to the Hodge diamond cutter: moduli of quiver representations. For every acyclic quiver and dimension vector, and suitable choice of stability condition, this produces a smooth projective variety, whose Hodge numbers are concentrated on the diagonal. The method to determine them is given by Corollary 6.9 in Markus Reineke's Inventiones paper.

Maybe I should spend some time discussing their geometry, but this will be it for now, interested readers are referred to this excellent article.

item.title: Two additions to the Hodge diamond cutter
item.description:
The functionality outlined below, and much more, is implemented in Hodge diamond cutter, which can be used in Sage. If you use it for your research, please cite it using .

Just a quick service announcement: I have now added Hodge diamonds for

  • the Fano varieties of $i$-dimensional linear subspaces on the intersection of $Q_1\cap Q_2\subset\mathbb{P}^{2g}$
  • the Grothendieck–Knudsen moduli space $\overline{M}_{0,n}$ of stable $n$-pointed rational curves

The first case, for $i=g-2$, is also the moduli space discussed in the previous post.

item.title: A DOI for the Hodge diamond cutter
item.description:
Back in January 2019 I released the Hodge diamond cutter, a convenient collection of Hodge diamonds of smooth projective varieties and methods to manipulate them. It's been extended since, and any suggestions for things to implement are still very welcome!

In the post-seminar conversation after a Zoom talk I gave in Hannover, someone brought up this software into the discussion, and Klaus Hulek suggested I'd get a DOI for it so that people can cite it accordingly. I have now done this, see for more information.

item.title: Some updates
item.description:
Here are some small updates, which do not deserve a blogpost of their own as such.

  • Hodge diamond cutter now also computes Hodge diamonds for Fano varieties of linear subspaces on the intersection of 2 quadrics. For more on this, see (the references in) this MathOverflow post where I learned that these are objects that one can study.

  • I have updated the conference schedule at ncag.info because of COVID-19 cancellations and postponements. Please let me know if I've missed something, or if your conference is not listed there.
